title: Draft: tcpdiff: a simple tool to match and compare TCP flows in two capture files
description:
The main driver of this work is the desire to save people some time.
And slightly simplify TCP analysis for people new to troubleshooting of
networking issues.
While RCA analysis itself, sometimes, could be slightly complicated, I
have noticed that some people struggle to map TCP streams in two files,
and, sometimes, give RCA analysis for two completely unrelated TCP
streams.

I would like get your opinion, feedback and comments, and general advice
and guidance. Does anybody find this useful?
Because, now, I use it every time I get two capture files from two
machines to analyze a networking issue.

To familiarize myself with the codebase/design of the project I tried to
reuse as much code as possible and make this patch as short as possible.
But there are some needed design changes if this work is to be merged
upstream.
For example, tshark cannot open two files simultaneously, and there are
global vars (like cfile) around that fact, and other subtle things.
It can all be changed, but for this RFC patch, I just want to get your
feedback on minimally viable product.

The utility workflow consists of five parts:
1. Read two capture files and get all TCP streams
2. Match TCP streams based on 5-tuple + time
3. Ask user which TCP stream he would like to analyze
4. Compare and diff TCP payloads from two files
5. Analyze termination (TCP FIN/RST) of the TCP stream

For #5 I have added two most common cases when active network hardware
between two machines interferes in the communication.
But more could be added later on.
a) both parties received TCP RST or TCP FIN, which means none of them
sent it, which means active network hardware did it.
b) TCP RST with payload, I haven't seen Linux/Windows kernel do it, and,
usually, active network hardware is to blame.

notes.body: this code needs a lot of work, closing for now, might come back to it later
